style: Say warmly with a gravelly voice, like an old park ranger telling stories
lines: Hmm, interesting… What does that clue tell us?
That’s every clue. Which natural resources did it come from?
Aha! Let’s follow the trail back to nature!
Clue one.
Clue two.
Clue three.
A new case! Where did this pencil come from? Let’s look for clues.
I started out tall and leafy, standing in a forest.
My dark middle came from deep inside the ground.
At a factory, my dark middle was glued between two strips of wood.
At a pencil factory, a dark stick of graphite is glued between strips of wood.
The wood comes from trees.
The dark graphite is a mineral dug out of rocks.
There’s the trail!
The pencil came from trees and rocks.
Try another case, and pick your guesses first.
Good detective work!
You found trees.
It also came from rocks.
Not quite!
It came from trees and rocks.
No plants in this one.
No water in this one.
No soil in this one.
You found rocks.
It also came from trees.
Case solved!
You found trees and rocks.
No animals in this one.
A new case! Where did this T-shirt come from? Let’s look for clues.
I grew in a sunny field.
I was white and fluffy, like a little cloud on a stem.
I was spun into thread, then woven and sewn.
Fluffy cotton is spun into thread, woven into cloth and sewn into a shirt.
Cotton is a plant. Its fluffy seed pods become thread.
The T-shirt came from plants.
It came from plants.
No trees in this one.
You found plants.
No rocks in this one.
A new case! Where did this orange juice come from? Let’s look for clues.
I grew on a tree in a warm, sunny place.
I was round and orange, and full of juice.
Then I was squeezed!
Oranges are picked from orange trees and squeezed into juice.
Oranges are the fruit of a plant.
The orange juice came from plants.
Yes! Orange trees are plants too.
Good thinking! The orange tree drank lots of water to grow its juicy fruit.
A new case! Where did this glass jar come from? Let’s look for clues.
I started as tiny grains on a beach.
I was melted in a fire much hotter than an oven.
Now you can see right through me.
Sand is melted in a very hot furnace and shaped into glass.
Sand is made of tiny bits of rock. Melted sand becomes glass.
The glass jar came from rocks.
It came from rocks.
A new case! Where did these wool mittens come from? Let’s look for clues.
I started out on the back of an animal.
Baa!
I was clipped off like a haircut, then spun and knitted.
Wool is clipped from sheep like a haircut, then spun into yarn and knitted.
Wool comes from sheep. It grows back, like hair.
The wool mittens came from animals.
It came from animals.
You found animals.
A new case! Where did this flower pot come from? Let’s look for clues.
I was dug out of the ground.
When I was wet, I was soft and squishy.
I was baked hard in a hot oven called a kiln.
Clay is dug from the ground, shaped on a potter’s wheel and baked hard.
Clay is a kind of soil.
The flower pot came from soil.
It came from soil.
Yes! Potters mix water into the clay to make it soft enough to shape.
You found soil.
Close! Clay forms from rocks that wore down over a very long time.
